research_question: Among pregnant women, new mothers, or other primary caregivers, what is the effect of oral-hygiene, diet, or feeding-practice advice, compared with standard care or no advice, on the risk that their children have caries in any primary tooth at the longest reported follow-up?
treatment_label: Oral-hygiene, diet, or feeding-practice advice delivered to pregnant women, new mothers, or other primary caregivers
outcome_description: Binary child-level presence of dental caries in any primary tooth at the longest follow-up reported: number of children with caries divided by number of children assessed in each arm. Use each trial's own caries definition and record it (e.g., any primary-tooth decay, dmft or dmfs >0, cavitated lesions, dentinal decay, or white-spot lesions), preferring the definition that captures any carious lesion in any primary tooth. Do not use outcomes restricted to a subset of teeth. Convert reported percentages to counts using the arm-specific number assessed; use the number randomized only when the assessed denominator is unavailable and flag this choice. Combine eligible advice intervention arms while counting a shared control only once; exclude intervention arms that add fluoride or another active dental treatment when an advice-only arm is available. For cluster-randomized trials, use an adjusted risk ratio or odds ratio as reported when available. Pool risk ratios using a random-effects model, with advice as the numerator and standard care/no advice as the denominator. Do not pool mean dmft/dmfs severity, tooth- or surface-level counts, restricted front-tooth outcomes, bacterial counts, behavior, knowledge, or adverse events.
positive_direction: A favorable treatment effect means fewer children have caries after caregiver advice than after standard care or no advice; on the requested ratio scale this corresponds to RR < 1 (if expressed as a positively oriented standardized effect, positive would mean the advice favors prevention of caries).
search_queries: caregiver oral hygiene diet feeding advice child dental caries randomized trial
pregnant women mothers caries prevention counselling controlled trial children primary teeth
motivational interviewing family centred oral health promotion early childhood caries trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomized controlled trials, including individually randomized and cluster-randomized trials, involving pregnant women, new mothers, or other primary caregivers of children with primary teeth or children subsequently followed into the primary dentition period.

Interventions broadly involving oral-hygiene, diet, or feeding-practice advice, counselling, motivational interviewing, family-centred health promotion, brushing/diet counselling, or feedback, compared with standard care or no advice.

Reports a quantitative child-level binary outcome for caries in any primary tooth at a follow-up time, or provides enough information to derive the number of children with caries and the number assessed.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study: systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, theoretical papers, protocols without results, and other non-empirical reports are excluded.
No comparison between an eligible advice treatment condition and a standard-care or no-advice control condition, including uncontrolled studies.

No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size: arm-level events and totals, convertible proportions, means plus SDs, t/F-values, proportions, odds ratios, or risk ratios are unavailable; for this specified binary outcome, studies reporting only mean dmft/dmfs, numbers of affected teeth/surfaces, or other non-child-level caries measures are excluded.

Completely unrelated to caregiver-delivered oral-hygiene, diet, or feeding advice and caries in children's primary teeth; also exclude fluoride-varnish-only or xylitol-only trials, arms that combine advice with an additional active treatment when no advice-only contrast is available, and studies reporting only restricted tooth subsets (such as the upper front four teeth), bacterial counts, behavior, knowledge, or adverse events.
moderators_to_extract: Caregiver group and timing of intervention delivery (pregnancy, postpartum/new mother, or other primary caregiver stage)
Advice modality/content (motivational interviewing, family-centred promotion, brushing advice, diet/feeding counselling, photograph-based feedback, or multicomponent advice)
Trial design and unit of randomization (individual versus cluster randomized)
Child age and duration of follow-up at outcome assessment
Trial-specific caries case definition and diagnostic threshold
Control condition (usual/standard care versus no advice)
effect_size_note: Primary synthesis: arm-level risk ratio (RR) for a child having caries, calculated as risk in the advice group divided by risk in the standard-care/no-advice group, and pooled with a random-effects model. RR < 1 favors advice. Use the longest follow-up per trial. Use children assessed as denominators, or children randomized if assessed counts are unavailable and document this. Convert percentages to integer event counts using arm-specific denominators with transparent rounding. Combine eligible advice-only arms and count a shared control once. For cluster-randomized trials, preferentially use the reported cluster-adjusted RR; if only an adjusted OR is reported, retain it as the reported adjusted effect rather than treating it as an unadjusted RR, and address metric compatibility explicitly in synthesis/sensitivity analysis. Record the exact caries definition used by each trial and prefer any-lesion/any-primary-tooth definitions.
single_outcome_target: presence of dental caries in any primary tooth
